question: Should ClawHub activate this signed sharded catalog protocol now, with its required DSSE key lifecycle and the dependent OpenClaw consumer still landing separately?
rationale: The patch creates a public signed distribution boundary and changes oversized skills compatibility; implementation tests cannot determine the intended rollout, trust-anchor, and consumer-support policy.

options.title: Stage behind consumer readiness
options.body: Keep the routes and producer capability inactive until the matching consumer and signing-key operating procedure are approved, then merge with explicit rollout proof.

options.title: Approve producer-first rollout
options.body: Merge the producer before consumer support, accepting that oversized legacy clients will receive the documented redirect and operators must provision signing keys first.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Defer public activation and retain only preparatory internal schema work in a smaller follow-up once the protocol direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Stage behind consumer readiness
recommendation.body: Keep the routes and producer capability inactive until the matching consumer and signing-key operating procedure are approved, then merge with explicit rollout proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed contributor across the active producer stack and can provide the concrete rollout and runtime evidence for maintainer review.
